citeAs: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (2025). VOICEASSISTANT-EVAL: BENCHMARKING AI ASSISTANTS ACROSS LISTENING, SPEAKING, AND VIEWING. arXiv.
creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK)
description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing, comprising 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories.
name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
publisher: CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK
rai:dataBiases: The questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts, which may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas.
rai:dataCollection: Visual and auditory inputs were extracted from 37 datasets. Texts from RoleBench were utilized to evaluate voice personalization. Speech instructions were synthesized using three advanced text-to-speech (TTS) models and evaluated with UTMOS. The synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper and compared to the original instructions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. Texts from RoleBench were also utilized.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has a monolingual focus (mostly English) which may not capture the full variability of real user interactions. It evaluates models in an offline, static manner, which might not capture practical deployment factors like latency constraints or continuous listening requirements. There are also gaps in task coverage and scenario realism, such as the absence of video-audio integration.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Special tokens in text were replaced with descriptive phrases. Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct was used to rewrite text to be more suitable for TTS (e.g., converting mathematical expressions and numbers to words). Multiple-choice options were rephrased for better readability.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Content was de-duplicated using lexical overlap and edit-distance matching. Incomplete or inappropriate items (missing/broken audio or images, ill-posed questions, incorrect answers) were filtered out. Remaining examples were mapped to 13 task categories with balanced sampling.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, which carries risks of identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. The authors prohibit training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent, and require downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended for researchers to use to better evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies in this area.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (for text rewriting), F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B (for speech synthesis), UTMOS Strong (for evaluating generated speech), Whisper-Large-v3 (for transcription)
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, which involves voice cloning of specific roles/speakers.
